battle.title: Split, Copy, Survive
battle.description: Shards, replicas, lag and quorums in a distributed data store.

questions.text: What is the difference between replication and sharding?
options: Replication splits data across nodes, sharding copies it
They are two names for the same technique
Sharding is only for caches, replication only for databases
Replication copies the same data to several nodes, sharding splits data into disjoint parts
questions.answer: Replication copies the same data to several nodes, sharding splits data into disjoint parts
questions.explanation: Replication gives redundancy and read capacity: every replica holds the same data. Sharding gives write and storage capacity: each shard holds a different slice. Real systems usually combine both.

questions.text: Users save their profile, reload, and sometimes see the old version because reads go to lagging replicas. What is the best fix?
options: Add more replicas to spread the reads
Send a user's reads to the leader for a short time after they write
Shard the profile table by user id
Make replication more asynchronous
questions.answer: Send a user's reads to the leader for a short time after they write
questions.explanation: This is read-your-writes consistency: the writer reads from the leader (or a caught-up replica) until replicas catch up. More replicas can increase lag, and sharding does not address staleness at all.

questions.text: An orders table is sharded by creation month. What problem will appear?
options: All current writes land on the newest shard, creating a hotspot
Old orders can no longer be found
Every query must touch all shards
Replication becomes impossible
questions.answer: All current writes land on the newest shard, creating a hotspot
questions.explanation: A monotonically increasing key such as time concentrates all new traffic on one shard while others sit idle. A high-cardinality, evenly spread key such as a hashed customer id spreads load better.

questions.text: Why use consistent hashing instead of hash(key) mod N to place keys on shards?
options: It removes the need for replication
It guarantees every shard holds exactly the same number of keys
Adding or removing a node moves only a small fraction of the keys
It makes lookups free of any network hop
questions.answer: Adding or removing a node moves only a small fraction of the keys
questions.explanation: With mod N, changing N remaps most keys. With a hash ring, a new node takes over only the neighbouring range (roughly 1/N of keys). Balance is helped by virtual nodes but never perfectly guaranteed.

questions.text: A store has N = 5 replicas. Which write quorum W and read quorum R guarantee that every read overlaps the latest successful write?
questions.explanation: Overlap needs R + W > N. 3 + 3 = 6 > 5 works. The other options each sum to exactly 5, so a read set can miss every node that holds the newest write.
